title: Bonds Looking Increasingly Comfortable With Recent Gains
summary:
Bonds Looking Increasingly Comfortable With Recent Gains 

             
             
            Much like last Friday, the stock market provided adequate cover for bonds to give back a decent chunk of recent gains. And much like Friday, bonds opted to hold fairly steady. Granted, there was certainly weakness after the 9:30am NYSE open, but not as much as you might expect given that stocks retraced more than half of last Thursday's losses. Part of the explanation could be due to lower oil prices, both in the overnight session and then again following war-related headlines in the 2pm ET hour.

title: Mortgage Rates Mostly Steady Despite Stock Market Bounce
summary: Last Thursday's stock market sell-off was a key factor in driving mortgage rates to the lowest levels in more than a month. More broadly, tech stock jitter have clearly correlated with multi-week trend toward lower rates that began in mid-October. As such, any time we see a pronounced bounce in stocks, we might be somewhat concerned about a similar bounce in rates.  Stocks definitely bounced today with both the S&P and NASDAQ retracing more than half of the losses seen last Thursday. Mortgage rates dropped 0.05% on Thursday, but  are only 0.01% higher today. One potential consideration is that oil prices continued even lower and that drop corresponded with lower bond yields at times.  The average top-tier 30yr fixed rate rose to 7.18%--the second lowest reading since September 14th.

title: Ops Efficiency, Non-QM, AI Governance Tools; M&A Strategy; Election Results and Lending; FEMA Changes
summary: All of you out there wishing there were fewer people on the roads or in line at the post office, take heart. Lenders with a long time horizon, not so much. Apparently, even paradise is having trouble keeping its population up: The Census Bureau released updated projections through 2100 for 25 countries and U.S. territories, revealing that population declines in American Samoa, Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands and the U.S. Virgin Islands are already underway and expected to continue through the century, alongside updated data for more than 16,600 regions worldwide. That doesn’t bode so well for home sellers or lenders, frankly. In other news impacting lenders and servicers, Bloomberg reports that FEMA stopped publishing key data on disaster aid. Not only that, but FEMA’s maps (some 20+ years old) undercount the U.S. flooding risk by about 6 million homes, many in Texas, Louisiana, and Florida, big lending areas. Are these good things for our nation? (More below.) (Today’s podcast can be found here. title: Slightly Weaker as Stocks Recover. CPI On Deck
summary: In the bigger picture, today offers little by way of actionable new info for the bond market. Unsurprisingly, volatility is being dictated by a decently big bounce in equities. Stocks were sideways to slightly stronger overnight, but have jumped somewhat sharply at the 9:30am NYSE open. Roughly half of last Thursday's rout has now been erased. Bonds weren't nearly as eager to move on Thursday relative to stocks and the same is true so far this morning. Tomorrow's CPI is the first major test this week. As for tail risk, a big enough bounce in stocks would likely not be great for bonds, if it happens (and it certainly could).

title: States Tighten Mortgage Rules For Home Equity Investments
summary: States are tightening their oversight of home equity financing arrangements that give investors a share of a property's future value, with Massachusetts becoming the latest to impose new requirements on certain shared-appreciation mortgages.A regulation that took effect Nov. 6 establishes disclosure, servicing, and reporting requirements for a specific category of shared-appreciation loans. It also defines when qualifying lenders can receive protection from certain consumer protection claims.

title: FICO vs. VantageScore: Lenders Gain More Options to Qualify Borrowers
summary: Mortgage lenders are beginning to put expanded credit score choice into practice, with credit reporting provider Informative Research reporting that its clients are actively using both Classic FICO and VantageScore 4.0 to evaluate mortgage applications.The Stewart-owned company announced Monday that it has upgraded its technology infrastructure to support multiple credit scoring models, allowing lenders to select a model for individual loans or obtain both scores on a single credit report.

title: Cash-Out Borrowers Leave Servicers Behind as Home Equity Hits Q3 Record
summary: American homeowners held $17.5 trillion in mortgage equity in the third quarter, but lenders and servicers are struggling to retain borrowers looking to tap that wealth, according to the latest ICE Mortgage Monitor.Servicers retained just 27% of refinancing borrowers during the quarter, down four percentage points from Q2, while cash-out refinances accounted for 75% of refinance-related loan losses to competitors, ICE reported Monday.

title: Mortgage Payments Rise 13% As Home Sales Slide: Zillow
summary: Home prices are barely rising, inventory is growing, and buyers have more negotiating power. Yet the cost of financing a home is moving in the opposite direction, leaving mortgage lenders facing an increasingly difficult purchase market.The typical monthly mortgage payment rose 12.8% year over year in October, even as home values increased just 0.7%, according to Zillow's October Market Report.
